articles.title: Global Market: PayPal takeover talks intensify as board mulls improved bid
articles.content: PayPal is reviewing a $53 billion takeover bid from Stripe and Advent International but considers the $60.50-per-share offer too low. Amid slowing growth, intense competition and repeated turnaround efforts, the board is weighing whether PayPal’s businesses—including Venmo—could unlock greater value separately or through a higher offer.

articles.content: Private investment will be crucial to funding Europe's growing defence industry as government budgets remain constrained, finance executives said at the Farnborough International Airshow. They stressed that public spending alone is insufficient and called for regulatory reforms.

articles.title: Global Market: Indonesia stocks attract bargain hunters as AI rally loses steam
articles.content: Global investors are shifting funds into Indonesia's stock market, which has seen significant declines. This rotation occurs as the rally in AI-linked stocks begins to lose momentum globally. Many portfolio managers are seeking undervalued markets with stronger long-term growth prospects. Analysts believe much of the negative news has already been reflected in current stock prices. Indonesia's market awaits a crucial MSCI decision in November, which could impact its status.

articles.title: Global Market:  Japan's Nikkei rebounds as bargain buying lifts stocks after sharp weekly selloff
articles.content: Japan's Nikkei share average advanced on Tuesday, recovering from last week's steep slide. Investors bought beaten-down stocks after a market holiday, boosting the index. Global sentiment remained cautious due to rising oil prices and inflation concerns. Focus now shifts to upcoming second-quarter earnings from major U.S. technology firms. Analysts noted the gains reflected a technical rebound ahead of key corporate results.

articles.title: South Korea’s Kospi jumps 4% after 31% crash from June peak. What’s ahead?
articles.content: South Korea's Kospi index saw a significant jump, recovering some losses after a sharp decline. Shares of chipmakers like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix drove this recent market recovery. However, the index remains in a bear market, reflecting investor caution and wild swings. Authorities have intervened to cool speculative fever and curb leveraged trading. Analysts suggest foreign investor selloffs are moderating, with a neutral stance on the market.

articles.title: Sensex falls over 50 points, Nifty below 24,250 despite Iran-US mediation efforts
articles.content: Indian stock markets saw marginal losses on Tuesday as Sensex and Nifty traded flat. Broader markets, however, opened with modest gains, bucking the overall trend. Geopolitical developments and regional tensions remain key factors influencing market sentiment.
